what_this_is: The measured bench data that the scheduling engine's pharmacology constants must be reconciled against, the constants themselves, and the reason the reconciliation is refused. Written by _run_bench_anchors.py; every measured number is engine-independent.

notes: 19 record(s) are right-censored ('>' relation: assay saturated below 50% effect). True IC50 is at least the reported bound. They are excluded from the point estimate and reported as a bound instead.

the exact-only median is biased low by selection (records are exact when the assay reached 50% effect, which correlates with greater potency); the true cohort median lies above median_lower_bound_nM and is not bounded above by these data
records span 2012-2025; assay and readout drift over that window is not controlled for
glioma_line_potency.describe: IC50 over 9 target(s): 31 exact (median 134,970 nM, most potent 6,426 nM, spread 496x), 19 right-censored (median lower bound 142,985 nM)
glioma_line_potency.unit_rule: mass-concentration records convert to molar ONLY through the molecule's molecular weight; anything unconvertible is counted in n_unconvertible_units and excluded from the point estimate

gdsc2_glioma_audit.verdict: 8384 glioma-row(s) over 286 drug(s) and 34 line(s); 76.0% of glioma IC50s lie above the highest concentration tested, and for temozolomide it is 34 of 34
gdsc2_glioma_audit.why_it_matters: a fitted IC50 above the plate's maximum tested concentration is a model extrapolation, not a measurement; those values are lower bounds and cannot anchor a kill constant

engine_constants.evidence_tier: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION -- not fitted to any measured kill rate. The engine's EC50 carries no concentration unit, so it cannot be compared to a molar IC50 at all; that refusal is the finding, not an omission to be papered over.

ec50_comparison.reason: the engine's EC50 has no declared concentration unit (DrugParams documents only 'conc/day at full-dose vessels'), so an EC50-vs-IC50 ratio would be unitless nonsense. Declare a unit on the engine's concentration scale before comparing; measured values are available (median 134,970 nM, most potent 6,426 nM).
ec50_comparison.describe: EC50 comparison REFUSED: the engine's EC50 has no declared concentration unit (DrugParams documents only 'conc/day at full-dose vessels'), so an EC50-vs-IC50 ratio would be unitless nonsense. Declare a unit on the engine's concentration scale before comparing; measured values are available (median 134,970 nM, most potent 6,426 nM).

reconciliation.verdict: REFUSED. The engine's kill constants remain authored assumptions. Public potency data exist and are measured, but they cannot be substituted into the engine as if they were kill rates.
blockers: TYPE: an IC50 is a concentration at 50% effect in a 2D monolayer at a fixed exposure time; the engine's kill_max is a per-day fractional kill rate in a 3D substrate with a diffusion gradient. Converting between them requires a rate-reporting (time-kill or clonogenic) assay, which is not in this tree.
UNIT: the engine's EC50 has no declared concentration unit, so any ratio between it and a molar IC50 is a type error rather than a fit (danon/pharmacology.py::compare_engine_ec50 refuses it).

CENSORING: 60 of temozolomide's 166 ChEMBL records are right-censored (the assay saturated below 50% effect), and GDSC2's glioma IC50s are largely extrapolated beyond the highest tested concentration -- the measured values are therefore bounded, and treating the bounds as exact points would import the assay's detection limit as pharmacology.
what_would_close_the_gap: A time-kill (or clonogenic surviving-fraction) assay on paired TMZ-sensitive and TMZ-resistant glioma lines reporting the net per-day kill rate at >= 4 concentrations.
The untreated growth rate of the same lines on the same substrate, so growth_S/growth_R are measured rather than assumed.
A tmz concentration axis in molar units, so a declared EC50 unit can be attached to the engine's parameters.
The same experiment for the second drug on the same line pair, which is what would make the drug-B marrow and potency assumptions measured instead of swept.

provenance.note: measured/curated inputs are ESTABLISHED at source; every quantity the engine actually consumes from them is UNKNOWN

cannot_prove: ChEMBL records come from different assays, readouts (ATP/MTT/clonogenic), exposure times and passage numbers, and most of that context is absent per record. Spread across them is methodological, so it is not reported as a standard error or a confidence interval.

Potency in 2D monolayer culture at 72 h is not potency in a 3D tumour with a diffusion gradient, an intact blood-brain barrier and heterogeneous sub-clones. No in-vitro IC50, however well measured, establishes in-vivo tumour kill.

Stokes-Einstein gives free-solution diffusion. In brain, binding, cellular uptake, efflux and convection dominate transport, and the derived D_eff is an upper bound on free transport rather than a tissue measurement.

The Clark logBB equation is a published QSAR fitted on a 1990s set with a substituted descriptor (ALogP for cLogP); its sign is informative, its magnitude is not reliable, and temozolomide is a known counterexample.
Nothing here validates the engine. These are measured pharmacology and derived transport bounds to calibrate against, not evidence that the scheduling model is right.
None of these three targets is a clinical endpoint. Spatial Dice and in-vitro IC50 agreement say nothing about a patient's outcome.
A high R^2 or Dice score on a shifted estimand cannot be added to, averaged with, or used to raise an overall-survival C-index.
The responder label that exists is a follow-up status flag, not a treatment response; scoring it well would not mean detecting responders.
GDSC glioma IC50s are largely extrapolations, so even a perfect fit to them would be a fit to a lower bound.
The engine's Hill slope is fixed at n=1 and has never been checked against measured dose-response curves.

The trained policy's reward is AUTHORED: it is fixed as minus the normalised burden curve so that training and reporting share one functional, but choosing burden over another quantity is a modelling choice no data can contradict. What the held-out evaluation can contradict is whether the policy keeps its recorded advantage.
EGFRvIII status is not obtainable from open GDC data, so it cannot be listed as a feature of a classifier built on this repository.
